question: What is the primary purpose of disease notification in public health?

options.A: To update personal medical insurance policies automatically
options.B: To determine hospital billing rates for infectious conditions
options.C: To trigger rapid public health containment measures
options.D: To fulfill mandatory facility accreditation requirements only

explanation: Prompt notification alerts health authorities so they can deploy containment strategies before outbreaks spread further. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why are private healthcare facilities legally required to report notifiable diseases?

options.A: To allow government agencies to audit private clinic finances
options.B: To ensure complete epidemiological data across the entire population
options.C: To standardize prescription pricing among different providers
options.D: To restrict private practitioners from treating severe infections

explanation: Diseases do not respect facility types, so total population tracking requires data from both public and private sectors. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h1)

question: What defines disease surveillance in public health practice?

options.A: Ongoing collection and analysis of health data
options.B: One-time screening during annual community outreaches
options.C: Emergency quarantine of all incoming international travelers
options.D: Routine disinfection of hospital surgical instruments

explanation: Surveillance is a continuous process of data gathering and interpretation rather than a single event. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h2)

question: How does tracking seasonal disease patterns assist health ministries?

options.A: By enabling proactive distribution of medical supplies before peaks occur
options.B: By setting mandatory international travel restrictions for citizens
options.C: By eliminating the need for community health education programs
options.D: By allowing clinics to close during predictable low-transmission months

explanation: Knowing when seasonal spikes happen lets authorities preposition drugs and protective gear ahead of time. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which condition requires immediate notification to public health authorities within 24 hours in Nigeria?
explanation: High-consequence pathogens like Lassa fever require immediate reporting due to their epidemic potential. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h3)

question: What distinguishes weekly routine reporting from immediate case notification?

options.A: Routine reports monitor endemic baseline trends rather than hyper-acute outbreaks
options.B: Weekly reports require international clearance from the World Health Organization
options.C: Immediate notification is only used for non-infectious chronic illnesses
options.D: Routine reports are handled exclusively by traditional village leaders

explanation: Endemic diseases with stable baseline numbers are tracked via periodic weekly summaries rather than emergency alerts. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h3)

question: Who is the primary local government officer responsible for receiving initial facility disease reports in Nigeria?

options.C: Chief Medical Director of the Teaching Hospital
options.D: Federal Minister of Health and Social Welfare

explanation: The DSNO operates at the LGA level to coordinate local surveillance and collect facility reports. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is a hierarchical reporting structure utilized for infectious disease data?

options.A: To ensure that community nurses never communicate directly with doctors
options.B: To increase administrative paperwork and slow down clinical workflows
options.C: To verify information and coordinate appropriate response levels systematically
options.D: To delay public awareness until political leaders approve announcements

explanation: Stepped reporting allows local validation and ensures higher tiers mobilize appropriate resources efficiently. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the name of the standardized framework used for disease surveillance reporting in many African nations including Nigeria?
explanation: IDSR is the overarching framework harmonizing public health surveillance activities across health tiers. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h5)

question: A community nurse completes a paper notification form for suspected cholera. Which action is most critical before dispatching the form to the DSNO?

options.A: Waiting for full autopsy results if the patient passes away
options.B: Translating the medical diagnosis into local traditional dialects for the file
options.C: Obtaining written permission from the patient's employer before submission
options.D: Ensuring patient demographics, symptom onset dates, and clinical details are fully recorded

explanation: Accurate clinical and demographic data are essential for epidemiologists to trace contacts and verify cases rapidly. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of an epidemiological outbreak investigation?

options.A: To redesign hospital architecture for better ventilation
options.B: To confirm the diagnosis and identify the source of transmission
options.C: To calculate individual patient treatment bills for insurance
options.D: To penalize healthcare facilities that missed early diagnoses

explanation: Investigations aim to verify the event and pinpoint where and how the pathogen is spreading. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why is field sample collection a critical step during a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: To provide definitive laboratory confirmation of the causative agent
options.B: To replace the need for physical patient physical examinations
options.C: To clear hospital waiting rooms of non-emergency visitors
options.D: To test new commercial cosmetics on local populations safely

explanation: Lab tests on biological specimens confirm the exact pathogen driving the cluster, guiding specific clinical therapy. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h6)

question: Where do community health nurses typically perform their primary surveillance duties?

options.B: Primary health clinics and rural outposts

explanation: Community nurses operate at the grassroots level in local clinics and rural health centers. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which responsibility is a key component of a community nurse's surveillance role?

options.A: Educating residents to recognize and report unusual illness clusters
options.B: Financing national epidemic preparedness budgets independently
options.C: Performing advanced genetic sequencing of viral mutations
options.D: Issuing international quarantine mandates for airline pilots

explanation: Community engagement and public health education empower local residents to spot and report suspicious symptoms early. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is a major barrier to effective disease reporting in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Poor internet connectivity and paper form stockouts
options.B: Zero incidence of infectious diseases in rural areas
options.C: Excessive availability of advanced genetic sequencing labs
options.D: Mandatory international travel for all primary nurses

explanation: Logistical constraints like broken logistics supply chains and poor digital infrastructure hinder rapid reporting. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h8)

question: How do feedback loops improve compliance with disease notification among frontline nurses?

options.A: By demonstrating that submitted data is analyzed and used to guide public health action
options.B: By replacing all human clinical staff with automated computer systems
options.C: By eliminating the need for any physical patient examinations
options.D: By fining clinics that fail to report at least ten cases every week

explanation: When nurses see how their reports contribute to national responses, motivation and reporting accuracy improve. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h8)
